head: claude/scope-overlap-self-attribution
title: scope-overlap: establish WHOSE declaration matched before calling it a collision
body:
## The defect

The scope-overlap audit compares a PR's changed files against every declared path on board #6927 and **never establishes whose declaration it matched**. It has fired nine times; six of those reported the reader's own START back at it.

That inverts the incentive the board exists to create: **following the protocol makes the alarm louder, and the cheapest route to a quiet audit is to declare nothing.** `CLAUDE.md` names the endpoint — *"an alarm that fires constantly and is routinely walked past is not background noise; the desensitized alarm is ITSELF a P1 bug."*

---

## OBSERVED — measured this session against primary sources

Board comments read from #6927; PR and branch state read from the GitHub API. Nothing below is inferred.

### 1. The dispatch called this "self-attribution". The mechanism is worse than that.

`issuecomment-5503070932` — the manager's own, deliberately precise START — contains **exactly one** backticked `claude/…` token. I ran the deployed collector's own regex against the verbatim body:

```
branchOf() -> 'claude/trading-system-workflow-design-1ln10f'
ALL backticked claude/ tokens in the manager's own START:
    claude/trading-system-workflow-design-1ln10f
session ids named: ['session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ']
```

That token appears **only in prose complaining that that session's declaration keeps matching it**:

> …every time attributing my files to the broad `docs/claude/work/` declaration made by `claude/trading-system-workflow-design-1ln10f` at 2026-09-01T11:59:53Z.

So the audit stamped an **innocent third party's branch name** onto the manager's own comment and reported it as a foreign declaration. That is not a self-match — it is a **fabricated attribution**, and strictly worse, because a reader can act on the name.

The script had already learned this exact rule for **paths** (the `Not touching:` inversion, still tested). It was never applied to **identity**.

### 2. A session is not a branch — branch equality could never have matched

| | |
|---|---|
| PR #10729 head ref | `claude/manager-state-0316` |
| Its board START's branch | `claude/trading-system-workflow-design-1ln10f` (mis-extracted) |
| Session id in both the START and the PR footer | `session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ` |

The manager posts one START per session and opens PRs from short-lived branches. Branch equality was structurally incapable of matching its own declaration **however precisely it declared**.

### 3. The staleness axis is REAL — I checked it, and it was total

The dispatch flagged this as unverified. Every declaring branch on #10731's audit (fired `2026-09-02T03:27:19Z`):

| declaring branch | its PR | merged at | before the audit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude/stray-oca-soak-writer` | #10640 | 09-01T06:26:46Z | ✅ 21h earlier |
| `claude/trading-system-workflow-design-1ln10f` | #10649 | 09-01T11:58:24Z | ✅ **90s before its own START was posted** |
| `claude/operating-layer-phase-c` | #10657 | 09-01T14:21:23Z | ✅ |
| `claude/claude-bot-drain-route` | #10674 | 09-01T21:36:38Z | ✅ |
| `claude/prop-fills-gap-20260901` | #10678 | 09-01T22:10:46Z | ✅ |
| `claude/claude-channel-registers` | #10685 | 09-02T01:11:28Z | ✅ |
| `claude/drain-perf-backlog-20260902` | #10717 | 09-02T02:00:39Z | ✅ |

**7 of 7 distinct branches, producing 8 of 8 attributed hits.** The `-1ln10f` START was posted *after* its own PR merged and then generated overlap reports for fifteen hours.

### 4. A fourth cause, found while reading

`issuecomment-5503056365`'s branch is `diag-pending-pings-delivered-read-surface` — **no `claude/` prefix**, which the old regex required. The live #10731 audit duly filed it `unattributable`. Now read correctly.

---

## INFERRED — stated separately, and deliberately not built on

- **"A merged PR means the session ended."** It does not, and I did not assume it. The manager merged 36 PRs in one night and kept working. So the new state is named **`other_landed`** — a claim about the *branch* — and its evidence string is emitted per hit rather than implied.
- **Whether the nine firings actually desensitised anyone.** Not measurable from here. The P1 argument rests on the repo's own precedent (202 of 376 CRITICAL rows from one un-latched alarm), not on a measurement of this detector.
- **Why the `-1ln10f` START was posted 90s after its PR merged.** Unknown. Recorded as a fact, not explained.

---

## The fix

Identity is now parsed **exactly like paths already were** — only from a self-identification context (the START line, or a `Session:`/`Branch:` label line), never from prose — keyed on **session id as well as branch**, and moved out of the workflow's JS into Python where it is unit-testable against the real comment.

**Four attribution states where there was one:**

| state | response |
|---|---|
| `mine` | suppressed — but **counted** in the footer, so over-suppression stays auditable |
| `other_active` | the headline. The real collision. |
| `other_landed` | its own section, evidence named. Says the **branch** landed, never that the session ended. |
| `unattributable` | preserved, still reported |

Three distinct headlines for three distinct facts, so a landed-only or unattributable-only match can no longer read as a live collision.

### The reporting bias is preserved throughout

Per the dispatch's instruction not to make the audit quieter in general:

- an **unknown** branch state, an **unreadable** PR list and an **unparsed** identity all resolve to `active`
- the `DONE` marker is **anchored to the first line** while `START` is not — deliberately asymmetric, because a false START only over-reports whereas a false DONE would **retire a live declaration**
- a `DONE` that predates its START does not retire it
- the **"declared by a START we could not attribute"** section is kept verbatim in spirit
- the **LOWER BOUND** caveat survives on *every* reporting render (tested on the landed-only path too)
- the three verdict states (`overlap`/`no_overlap`/`could_not_check`) are untouched

---

## Both-direction controls

Replayed end-to-end through the CLI on **verbatim board comments**, with the real merge states above.

**A. The live #10729 case** — deployed audit headlined **6** foreign declarations:

```
### ℹ️ scope-overlap audit — PR #10729 touches files whose declaring branch has since landed
**No live collision.** …
_Compared 3 changed file(s) against 18 declared path(s) — 0 from a live session,
 3 from a landed branch, 0 unattributable, 3 matched your OWN declaration and were not reported._
```

**B. A genuine cross-session overlap on the same board** (a drain session's PR touching the file the manager exclusively claimed) — **still fires**:

```
### ⚠️ scope-overlap audit — PR #99001 touches files a LIVE session declared
- `docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json` — declared as `docs/claude/work/` by
  [`session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ`](…#issuecomment-5503070932) at 2026-09-02T01:42:42Z
_… 2 from a live session, 0 from a landed branch, 0 unattributable, 0 matched your OWN declaration._
```

Note line 2 of **B**: the manager's START is now attributed to **its actual session**, where the deployed audit named an innocent branch.

**Tests:** self-test **34 → 60** planted controls (the guard CI runs) + **23** new pytest cases in `tests/test_scope_overlap_attribution.py`, including one that pins the *old* regex's wrong answer so a revert cannot pass quietly.

---

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py --self-test` | 60/60 |
| `pytest tests/test_scope_overlap_attribution.py` | 23 passed |
| `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` (**run after committing**) | **PASS 45 · FAIL 1 · SKIP 24** |

The one failure is **`layer-guard: lint-imports … exited 127`** — the binary is not installed in this sandbox (`which lint-imports` → not found; it fails identically on untouched `origin/main`). `.importlinter` declares `root_package = src` and this diff touches no `src/`. **Not weakened, not skipped — flagged for CI to settle.**

Full-suite collection shows **111 errors on my branch and 111 on untouched `origin/main`** — all missing third-party deps here (pandas ×47, numpy ×20, …). My file contributes **zero**; the branch adds 22 collected tests (12604 → 12626).

---

## What I deliberately did NOT change, and why

- **The audit still comments on a landed-only match.** It could have gone silent and been quieter still. The dispatch was explicit that suppressing a real overlap is the worse error and that labelling is the sanctioned remedy, so landed matches are **relabelled, not silenced** — those files did move under you.
- **`collapsed-state-guard` registration.** The four states live in a pure function whose self-test is already a registered guard; that table targets producer/consumer pairs **across modules**, and registering a single-module vocabulary would invite the decorative branch it exists to prevent. Flagged rather than done — reverse it if you disagree.
- **`_START_RE` left loose.** Only `_DONE_RE` was anchored. A false START over-reports (safe); a false DONE suppresses (not safe). Tightening both would have been symmetry for its own sake.
- **The 24h lookback.** Untouched. Staleness is now graded, so widening it is a separate decision with separate evidence.
- **Nothing in scope-restricted territory.** No backlog file, no `OPEN-ITEMS.json`, no `docs/claude/work/`, no `config/`, no `ROADMAP.md`, no order path.

### One declared residual, pinned rather than hidden

`pr_session_ids` trusts that a `claude.ai/code/session_…` URL in a PR body is that PR's own footer. A body **quoting** another session's footer (a pasted handoff prompt) would adopt that identity and suppress its declaration. The alternatives are worse — taking only the last URL breaks on any note appended after the footer; harvesting bare `session_…` tokens is far worse, since PR #10729's body names two sub-sessions it spawned. Documented in the function, **asserted by `test_the_quoted_footer_residual_is_pinned_not_latent`**, and bounded: the audit gates nothing, so the most such a body buys is a quieter advisory comment on the author's own PR.

---

## FOR THE MANAGER

1. **This PR is a live instance of the bug it fixes.** My own board START (`issuecomment-5503965766`) will have generated an overlap report on this PR, as the dispatch predicted. Worth reading beside the fix.

2. **Backlog row text — I could not file it** (three drains are live on those files and they are out of my scope). Please place in `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json`:

   > **`BL-20260902-SCOPE-OVERLAP-ATTRIBUTES-A-BRANCH-NAMED-IN-PROSE`** — The scope-overlap collector resolved "whose START is this?" with `body.match(/`(claude\/[^`\s]+)`/)` — the first backticked branch **anywhere** in the body. On `issuecomment-5503070932` (the manager's own precise START) the only such token was **another session's branch, quoted in prose complaining about it**, so the audit reported a fabricated attribution to a named third party. Nine benign firings, six of them self-matches. The same class had already been fixed for PATHS (`Not touching:`) and never applied to IDENTITY. Fixed in PR on `claude/scope-overlap-self-attribution`. ⚠️ **The transferable lesson is the general one:** a mechanism that decides *whose* something is by grepping a token out of prose will attribute it to whoever the prose is ABOUT.

   > **`BL-20260902-A-BOARD-DECLARATION-NEVER-GOES-STALE`** — A `START` on #6927 goes on matching forever. Measured on #10731's audit: **7 of 7** declaring branches had already merged, one of them **90 seconds before its own START was posted**, and it kept generating overlaps for 15h. Now graded via branch PR state + `DONE` posts, failing toward `active`. ⚠️ **A merged PR is NOT proof the session ended** — the new state is called `other_landed` for that reason.

3. **Two open questions for you, neither blocking:**
   - Should a **landed-only** match comment at all, or write to the job summary only? I chose to comment (relabelled) because silencing is the riskier direction; you may prefer quieter.
   - The `-1ln10f` START posted **90s after its own PR merged** is still open on the board. I did **not** post a `DONE` on its behalf — that would put a false record on the board, and the manager's own START says the same. It wants a `DONE` from whoever can attest to it.

4. **`layer-guard` (127)** is the only red locally and is a missing binary here, not a finding. Confirm it passes in CI before merging rather than taking my word for it.
